charts.editorial_rationale: WTI's war-driven climb from roughly US$62/bbl in early February to US$103.02 on May 19, holding above the US$100 mark the writers repeatedly cite as the fuel-cost reference, is the dominant story this edition. The spatial relationship between the price line and the US$100 level — and how the rally drove the record +28.6% gasoline contribution to April CPI — is what prose only approximates.
charts.callout_text: The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links sustained WTI above US$100/bbl to 672 fuel-cost-exposed projects ($141.71B): 59 oil_gas projects ($97.58B) and 613 transport_logistics projects ($44.13B). The same crude path drove the record +28.6% year-over-year gasoline contribution that lifted April CPI to +2.8%.

charts.editorial_rationale: The equities writer flags a divergence — the S&P/TSX Composite fell -0.72% on the week to 33,833 while the S&P 500 and Dow rose more than 6% — after the resource complex peaked mid-week and the April CPI print firmed BoC-hold expectations. The intra-period peak-and-fade is a shape the per-index narrative states but cannot show.
charts.callout_text: The TSX rose to 34,291 on May 12 before fading to 33,833 by May 15 as the loonie eased to 0.7264 and the +2.8% April CPI print firmed BoC-hold expectations. The cross-reference engine ties the resource weighting to 390 mining projects ($227.11B) and 59 oil_gas projects ($97.58B).
